name: Non-syndromic Preaxial Polydactyly

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Non-syndromic Preaxial Polydactyly

criteria.description: Presence of an additional digit on the preaxial (radial/thumb) side of the hand or foot
Lack of associated systemic or syndromic abnormalities such as craniofacial, cardiac, or neurological anomalies
Radiographic evidence showing well-formed extra digit with normal bone structure
Positive family history of isolated preaxial polydactyly supports diagnosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of an extra preaxial digit confirmed clinically and radiographically, with exclusion of syndromic features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may identify mutations in GLI3 or other related genes but is not mandatory for diagnosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Preaxial polydactyly (extra thumb or great toe)
pathognomonic.notes: Typically unilateral or bilateral duplication of the thumb or big toe
searchTerms: additional digit on thumb or great toe side
extra finger or toe on preaxial side

pathognomonic.symptomName: Well-formed extra digit with normal bone segmentation
pathognomonic.notes: Extra digit usually fully developed and functional
searchTerms: extra digit with normal bone segments
well-formed extra finger or toe bones
complete bone structure in extra digit

common.notes: Partial webbing or fusion of skin between digits
searchTerms: soft tissue connection between duplicated digits

common.symptomName: Normal motor function of affected limb
common.notes: No functional impairment in most cases
searchTerms: normal movement and strength in affected limb
no motor problems in hand or foot with extra digit
intact muscle function in affected arm or leg

occasional.symptomName: Mild joint stiffness in duplicated digit
searchTerms: slight joint stiffness in extra finger
mild limited movement in duplicated digit joint

occasional.symptomName: Cosmetic concerns related to extra digit
searchTerms: concerns about appearance of extra finger
worries about cosmetic look of extra digit
psychological impact from extra finger or toe

occasional.symptomName: Minor nail abnormalities on duplicated digit
searchTerms: small nail changes on extra finger
minor nail defects on extra digit

rare.symptomName: Mild pain or discomfort in duplicated digit
rare.notes: Usually related to trauma or overuse
Rarely due to friction or pressure

searchTerms: slow bone growth in extra finger
delayed bone hardening in duplicated digit
late bone development in extra finger

imaging: Radiographs showing well-formed extra digit with normal bone segmentation on preaxial side
Absence of bone abnormalities or syndromic skeletal malformations
genetic: Mutations in GLI3 gene associated with isolated preaxial polydactyly
Other loci including ZRS enhancer mutations implicated
other: Physical examination confirming isolated preaxial digit duplication
Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance pattern

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of systemic anomalies such as craniofacial, cardiac, or neurological defects
Polydactyly associated with syndromic features like Greig cephalopolysyndactyly syndrome
Extra digit located on ulnar/fibular side rather than preaxial side
Different genetic causes and inheritance patterns

redFlags: Presence of additional congenital anomalies suggesting syndromic polydactyly
Rapidly progressive swelling or ulceration of duplicated digit
references: Klopocki E, et al. GLI3 mutations cause isolated preaxial polydactyly. Hum Genet. 2008.
Temtamy SA, McKusick VA. The Genetics of Hand Malformations. 1978.
